checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average (224 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: entry_granularity_declared (ok=true): "Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel" — the +0.54pp pump overstatement is declared harmless for between-arm verdicts.
findings.problem: That defence only holds for arms whose changed parameter is orthogonal to the bias. entry-8pct's changed parameter IS pump_pct=8.0, measured on the same quantity the kernel reads 0.54pp too large across 224 matched setups, so the arm is not testing an 8.0 threshold on the live population at all — its detection set is systematically looser than the row states. vol-4x sits on the same class of concern. The blanket 'stays valid' sentence is attached to every surfaced verdict, including one it does not cover.

findings.claim: entry-8pct screen_dWR=0.0pp and vol-4x screen_dWR=0.0pp — the same value carried by placebo, which the placebo_inert check proves is exactly inert (b=0, c=0).
findings.problem: Those two arms report screen_wr=51.807 (n=498) and 51.487 (n=874) against control's 50.128 (n=1560), so a delta-WR field reading exactly 0.0pp is not describing their screen numbers. Reduced-sample arms appear to be silently defaulted to zero rather than paired, which makes a real difference indistinguishable from the placebo's provable inertness in the one column a reader scans for effect size. The field is also unreconciled elsewhere: tp-7pct shows -3.41pp against screen_wr=46.594 vs control 50.128, and hold-12h 3.27pp against 53.423 vs 50.128.

findings.claim: paired_population (ok=true): "Every arm scored on identical events — 4848 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them."
findings.problem: The detail itself lists a different open-trade exclusion per arm (control 14, hold-12h 11, tp-7pct 18, vol-4x 10), and those exclusions track the exit parameter under test: shorter max_hold_h resolves trades faster and so scores more of them, longer tp_pct leaves more unresolved. Seeing the same events is not being scored on the same events. The censoring is correlated with the treatment for exactly the arms (hold-12h, tp-7pct) whose treatment is time-to-exit, and the checkbox title asserts something stronger than its own detail establishes.

findings.claim: no_lookahead (ok=true, critical): "Detection is look-ahead free — re-detected 108 events on truncated history across 6 coins; mismatches: none."
findings.problem: 108 events is a small fraction of the 4848 in the shared window, and 6 coins a small fraction of the 176 monitored. A clean re-detection on that slice is consistent with look-ahead freedom but does not establish it for the universe the arms actually trade — and the coins where the kernel is known to disagree with the live bot (BOME on four setups, BANANA) are precisely the kind of name the sample would need to include. LA is the project's own first-listed failure mode; a green critical box should not rest on a sample this thin without the coverage being stated as a limitation.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is listed as [running/confirm], i.e. an arm progressing toward the planned confirm n=600.
findings.problem: It has live_n=5 with declined=79 of the 84 live events — it is declining roughly nineteen in twenty detections, and it is the only arm with negative screen EV (-0.035, n=498). At that acceptance rate the confirm bar is not reachable on any horizon this arena has data for (63.0 days of candles, 84 live events total), yet the status string reads identically to hold-12h at live_n=26. Reporting it as running/confirm presents a sample it cannot accumulate as a test in progress, and it occupies a slot while doing so.

findings.claim: MECHANISM CLASSES: "one per running arm — diversity is enforced in code."
findings.problem: The arena contradicts this on two classes at once: entry_trigger is held by both control (changed={}) and entry-8pct, and liquidity_filter by both placebo (min_price=1e-12) and vol-4x. Either the enforcement does not run on control/placebo, or the class labels on the running arms are not the thing being enforced. Both readings matter, because the diversity rule is what stops the arena from spending its 6-test lifetime budget re-asking one question, and control being labelled entry_trigger at all makes the class field unreliable as an audit surface.
